message.content:
The three most significant schisms in Christian history are:

| # | Schism | Approximate Date | Key Parties Involved | Main Causes |
|---|--------|------------------|----------------------|-------------|
| 1 | **Great Schism (East–West Schism)** | 1054 CE | Roman Catholic Church (West) vs. Eastern Orthodox Church (East) | Doctrinal differences (e.g., the Filioque clause), ecclesiastical authority, cultural and linguistic divides, and political tensions between the Papacy and the Patriarchate of Constantinople. |
| 2 | **Protestant Reformation** | 1517–1648 CE | Roman Catholic Church vs. various Protestant movements (Lutheranism, Calvinism, Anglicanism, etc.) | Accusations of corruption and abuses in the Catholic Church, theological disputes over justification, the authority of Scripture vs. tradition, and the rise of vernacular translations and printing technology. |
| 3 | **East–West Schism of 1965 (also called the “Second East–West Schism” or “Modern Schism”)** | 1965 CE | Roman Catholic Church vs. the Orthodox Church of the former Soviet Union (and some other Orthodox jurisdictions) | Political pressures during the Cold War, differing responses to the Soviet regime, and disputes over the status of the Orthodox Church in the USSR. |

These three events represent the most profound and lasting divisions within Christianity, each reshaping the religious, cultural, and political landscapes of their times.
